10.1016_j.ijhydene.2025.05.143: This study focuses on the potential valorization of brewers' spent grain (BSG) through gasification for ultra-pure green hydrogen production via membrane separation. First, a fundamental physicochemical characterization of BSG samples from two different Spanish brewing industries was conducted, revealing high energy content and good reproducibility of elemental composition, thus providing great potential for hydrogen generation in the context of circular economy for the brewery industry. The syngas composition reached by BSG gasification has been predicted and main operating conditions optimized to maximize the hydrogen yield (25–75 vol% air-steam mixture ratio, GR = 0.75, T = 800 °C and P = 5 bar). For gas purification, two Pd-membranes were fabricated by ELP-PP onto tubular PSS supports with high reproducibility (Pd-thickness in the range 8.22–8.75 μm), exhibiting an almost complete H 2 -selectivity, good fitting to Sieverts’ law and hydrogen permeate fluxes ranging from 175 to 550 mol m −2 h −1 under ideal gas feed composition conditions. The mechanical resistance of membranes was maintained at pressure driving forces up to 10 bar, thus highlighting their potential for commercialization and industrial application. Furthermore, long-term stability tests up to 75 h indicated promising membrane performance for continuous operation, offering valuable insights for stakeholders in the brewery industry to enhance economic growth and environmental sustainability through green hydrogen production from BSG. • Technical feasibility of H 2 -production via BSG gasification and membrane separation. • High reproducibility of ELP-PP membrane fabrication with Pd-thickness below 10 μm. • Membranes stability for continuous operation at 450 °C and pressures up to 10 bar. • Almost complete H 2 -selectivity and permeances in the range 175–550 mol m −2 h −1 .
10.1016_j.memsci.2025.123896: The introduction of zwitterionic polymers into porous membranes is an important technique for imparting antifouling properties. However, the lack of methods for modifying polymer layers with controlled physical characteristics on inert membrane pores has resulted in an incomplete evaluation of how polymer structure and density affect fouling properties. This study aims to address this issue by creating reactive groups through a thin layer of precoated polydopamine (PDA), followed by polymer immobilization using a density-controllable click reaction that takes polymer–solvent interactions into account. The proposed method facilitates the formation of a durable PDA layer through thermal annealing at a moderate temperature. A grafting-to approach is used for polymer immobilization, which usually leads to a low graft density; however, polymer density can be controlled in the brush region by changing the reaction solvent. This study demonstrates the high reproducibility and accuracy of this membrane modification method using various characterization techniques. Additionally, the impact of polymer density on antifouling performance is assessed through dynamic fouling tests. • Density-controllable grafting-to approach on a polydopamine (PDA) coated membrane enables precise polymer modification. • The low durability of PDA resulting from insufficient polymerization is addressed through thermal annealing of the membrane. • The impact of density of the zwitterionic polymer brush on antifouling performance is assessed through dynamic fouling tests.
10.1021_acscatal.5c06754: Electrocatalyst nanoparticles, attached to an electronically conductive support material, are key components determining the performance and lifetime of electrochemical devices like fuel cells and electrolyzers. Differences in intrinsic (electronic) properties between nanoparticle and support induce phenomena subsumed as electro–ionic metal–support interactions. These phenomena are responsible for heterogeneously distributed electron densities and electrical double layer properties along the surface. The resulting local reaction environment, qualitatively different from that of single-crystalline extended surfaces, remains poorly understood. In an effort to address this shortcoming, the current work introduces a novel descriptor for the local reaction environment, namely the effective proton concentration. This descriptor can be obtained theoretically by averaging the proton concentration over the reaction plane around supported nanoparticles. Using gold-supported silver nanoparticles as a model system, we have investigated how the effective proton concentration depends on the size and the density of nanoparticles, Fermi levels of nanoparticle and support materials, bulk electrolyte concentrations, and electrode potential. Results will be discussed in view of the suitability of this effective parameter to be used in the design and optimization of supported nanoparticle-based electrocatalysts for electrochemical applications.
10.1038_s41467-026-71443-7: Monitoring neural population activity at single-cell resolution is essential for fundamental research and clinical innovation. However, translating advanced recording techniques from animal models to humans remains a challenge. Flexible neural electrodes have emerged as powerful tools for large-scale single-unit recordings due to their biocompatibility and high recording density. Here, we demonstrate reliable, high-density single-unit recordings during intraoperative procedures in human patients using ultra-Flexible Implantable Neural Electrode (uFINE) arrays. The uFINE array exhibited sufficient mechanical robustness to maintain structural integrity throughout surgical operations. We successfully recorded 719 single units from 11 patients, with up to 135 single units simultaneously recorded. The flexibility of uFINE array minimized signal disturbances from brain pulsations, enabling stable and continuous single-unit detection. Stimulus and response tuning were observed at the level of individual neurons in awake patients. Achieving high-density single-neuron recordings in humans is challenging. Here, the authors demonstrate a flexible implantable neural electrode array that enables reliable single-unit recordings in human patients during surgery
10.1039_d5cc00018a: The positively charged sites resulting from electronic redistribution in the metal phosphate heterostructures lead to reduced energy barriers, demonstrating an effective strategy for OER catalysts with low overpotentials and remarkable stability.
10.1039_d6ta04046b: This review provides a comprehensive perspective on organo-sulfur chemistry in perovskite solar cells, focusing on how sulfur functional groups regulate crystallization, passivate defects, and stabilize interfaces to enhance photovoltaic performance.
10.3390_ani15040562: Nanoplastics (NPs) can cross cellular membranes and affect cellular performance. This study aims to determine the effects of polystyrene NPs (PS-NPs, 44 nm) on gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata) exposed for 14 days to 100 μg/L PS-NPs. The results show that biometric indicators (weight, length, Fulton’s condition factor, and hepatosomatic index) were not affected after the experimental exposures. No significant effects were observed on white blood cell count, red blood cell count, mean corpuscular hemoglobin, or platelets compared to the control group. However, there was a significant decrease in hemoglobin concentration, hematocrit values, and mean corpuscular cell volume in fish exposed to PS-NPs. There were no significant effects on plasmatic cholesterol, triglyceride, alkaline phosphatase, or aspartate aminotransferase levels. The histological anatomy of both the gills and the intestine revealed no obvious signs of cellular damage, excessive mucous, or inflammation in the PS-NP group. The expression of transcripts related to lipid metabolism (pparα, pparβ), growth and development (igf1), detoxification (bche), and oxidative stress (sod, gpx1) were significantly downregulated in animals exposed to PS-NPs, indicating a slight impairment in lipid homeostasis and antioxidant response.
